import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert categorical variables into numerical
le = LabelEncoder()
customer_segments['Education'] = le.fit_transform(customer_segments['Education'])
customer_segments['Marital_Status'] = le.fit_transform(customer_segments['Marital_Status'])

# Split the data into numerical and categorical variables
numerical_vars = customer_segments.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns
categorical_vars = customer_segments.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns

# Scale the numerical data
scaler = StandardScaler()
customer_segments[numerical_vars] = scaler.fit_transform(customer_segments[numerical_vars])

# Pairplot to visualize the relationship between numerical variables
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.pairplot(customer_segments[numerical_vars])
plt.title('Pairplot of Numerical Variables')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Histograms to visualize the distribution of numerical variables
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.histplot(customer_segments['Income'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Income')
plt.xlabel('Income')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.savefig('income_histogram.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Barplot to visualize the distribution of categorical variables
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.countplot(x='Education', data=customer_segments)
plt.title('Distribution of Education')
plt.xlabel('Education')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.savefig('education_barplot.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Boxplot to visualize the distribution of numerical variables by categorical variable

sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Income', data=customer_segments)
plt.title('Boxplot of Income by Education')
plt.xlabel('Education')
plt.ylabel('Income')
plt.savefig('income_boxplot.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
